newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet sale still on course - Italian govt.
newsitem.headline: Stet sale still on course - Italian govt.

text.p: The privatisation of telecom holding company Stet will go ahead as planned in the Spring of 1997 so long as parliament approves a bill setting up a watchdog body for the sector by year-end, the post ministry undersecretary said.

"If the bill is ratified, as expected, by the end of the year, there is no reason why the privatisation should not go ahead between the beginning of February and the end of March 1997," Vincenzo Vita told Reuters.
"People who have doubts about the Stet privatisation should not use the timetable of the authorities' bill as an excuse (to prevent it)," Vita said.
Last Friday, Stet managing director Ernesto Pascale said that if the watchdog authority was not approved by the end of November, there would not be time to float Stet by March.
The authority bill is tied to a draft law covering television ownership, which is hotly disputed by the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance bloc in parliament.

Pascale said he wanted Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico to strip out the section relating to the regulatory body and hasten its progress through parliament to ensure the Stet privatisation kicked off on schedule.
